---
title: "regmatches() drops the strings with no match"
ref: STR-02
categories: [Strings]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`\"1\" NA \"333\"`, one result per string"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
texts <- c("a1b22", "none", "c333")
regmatches(texts, m = regexpr("[0-9]+", text = texts))
regmatches(texts, m = gregexpr("[0-9]+", text = texts))
```
:::

## Why

Base R has no "extract" function: you have to combine a function that finds the positions (`regexpr()` for the first match, `gregexpr()` for all of them) with `regmatches()`, which cuts the text at those positions.

With `regexpr()`, `regmatches()` only returns the matches it found. `"none"` vanishes without a warning: the result has two elements for three texts, and no longer lines up with them. Dropped into a data frame column, it gets recycled or triggers a length error far from its cause. With `gregexpr()`, you get a list, where a missing match is a `character(0)`.

## The fix

`stringr::str_extract()` returns one value per string, with `NA` when nothing matches. `str_extract_all()` gives the list of all matches.

::: {.piege packages="stringr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stringr))

str_extract(texts, pattern = "[0-9]+")
str_extract_all(texts, pattern = "[0-9]+")
```
:::
